poster_title: AQA: Adaptive Question Answering in a Society of LLMs via Contextual Multi-Armed Bandit
authors: Mohanna Hoveyda, Arjen P. de Vries, Maarten de Rijke, Harrie Oosterhuis, Faegheh Hasibi
paper_info: Radboud University, Nijmegen, The Netherlands; University of Amsterdam, Amsterdam, The Netherlands

panels.headline: Different questions require different answering strategies
content: Complex QA systems with multiple modules can enhance performance but increase computational costs.
Graph-based orchestration of LLMs has been proposed to optimize information flow between models.
There is a need for adaptive QA frameworks that dynamically adjust to varying question characteristics.
Complex LLM-based QA systems do not always improve performance and can be computationally expensive.
AQA is designed to balance performance and computational efficiency.

panels.headline: Complex LLM-based QA systems do not always improve performance
content: Current complex QA systems are not always effective and can be resource-intensive.
There is a need for a more adaptive and efficient approach to QA.
AQA addresses this by dynamically selecting the most suitable answering strategies.

panels.headline: AQA framed as a contextual multi-armed bandit (CMAB) problem
content: AQA uses a CMAB to select the most suitable answering strategy per question.
A context vector x_t represents question features, guiding the CMAB's decisions.
A linear upper confidence bound model is trained to learn the optimal mapping between question types and communication graph configurations.
panels.figure_caption: LinUCB expected rewards for individual agents action space, dashed lines depict the real rewards per action.

panels.headline: Evaluated on multi-complexity-level QA dataset
content: The AQA framework is evaluated on a dataset with varying levels of question complexity.
Performance and inference cost are balanced using a reward function that considers both effectiveness and efficiency.
Table 1 shows the performance of each individual agent on the training set.
panels.figure_caption: Performance of each individual agent on the training set (by F1-score and average time in seconds).

panels.headline: AQA optimizes performance and computational efficiency
content: AQA successfully recognizes and applies the most suitable answering strategies for different question types.
The framework optimizes both performance and computational efficiency.
panels.figure_caption: LinUCB expected rewards for the collaborative action space, dashed line depicts real reward for the optimal action.

panels.headline: AQA is a viable framework for adaptive QA systems
content: AQA is a viable framework for adaptive orchestration of QA systems, combining high performance and low computational costs.
The CMAB approach provides a flexible and effective way to dynamically select the most suitable answering strategies.
The framework's performance may be limited by the quality and features of the context vector.
AQA is a significant step towards more efficient and adaptive QA systems.
The approach can be extended to other multi-agent LLM-based systems.
